text: In a single-photon source, the Purcell effect is exploited to:
choices: Enhance the emitter's spontaneous-emission rate into the desired cavity mode, raising the collectable fraction beta and shortening the lifetime
Slow the emitter down so photons are emitted less often
Cool the quantum dot to its ground state
Convert the photon's wavelength to 1550 nm
explanation: The Purcell effect (F_P = (3/4pi^2)(lambda/n)^3 Q/V) speeds emission into the resonant cavity mode; beta = F_P/(F_P+1) saturates quickly (F_P = 10 gives beta = 0.91), and the shortened lifetime also boosts indistinguishability and rate. It accelerates, not slows, emission (choice 1); it is not a cooling (choice 2) or wavelength-conversion (choice 3) mechanism.
